target_customer: Spreadsheet users who want Python (data scientists, analysts and Excel users)
problem: Spreadsheets cannot be programmed with a real language; users move between Excel and notebooks.
business_model: Freemium SaaS spreadsheet and Google Sheets add-on

founders.name: Douwe Osinga
previous_startups: Founder of 4 companies (not named on YC page)
founders.background_notes: Wrote a book on deep learning.

competitors.name: Actiondesk
competitors.what: Spreadsheet connected to live business data

competitors.name: Equals
competitors.what: Spreadsheet platform with live data integrations

technical_complexity.rationale: A spreadsheet engine with a sandboxed Python kernel and AI assistance is standard engineering with some hard parts for a four-person team.

defensibility.rationale: Spreadsheet incumbents could add Python; Microsoft launched Python in Excel in 2023 (per The New Stack).

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Microsoft launched Python in Excel in August 2023, five months after the TechCrunch launch coverage (The New Stack, Oct 2023).

market_need_then: Demand signal is thin: no revenue at the March 2023 TechCrunch article, Hacker News launch Feb 2023, and the company says users made thousands of spreadsheets.

brand_strength.rationale: Invented name with no sourced meaning or brand coverage; nothing shows community or merch.

outcome_analysis: Neptyne launched in 2022-23 as a Python spreadsheet, raised a $2M pre-seed in March 2023 and shipped a Google Sheets add-on, then Microsoft announced Python in Excel in August 2023. YC lists the company as Inactive, but no shutdown notice, post-mortem or acquisition announcement was verified, so the cause and form of the end are not public.
notes: YC status Inactive but no source found for a shutdown, so exit.type is unknown.
